clue.text: To cancel, one rings

parts.note: to annul something is to cancel or void it
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A puzzling instruction pairing the act of cancelling with someone who rings, like a bell-ringer calling off a peal.
explanation.definitionFit: Annuli is the plural of annulus, a ring-shaped figure in geometry or anatomy.

clue.text: Broadcast from underworld with acclaim

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and by extension the underworld itself
a tribute is praise or acclaim

explanation.surface: Something transmitted from the underworld to great applause.
explanation.definitionFit: To broadcast seed or news is to scatter or spread it around, the verb sense.

clue.text: Demoralised, like the Tories with Theresa gone?

definitions.text: like the Tories with Theresa gone
definitions.meaning: the Conservatives once Theresa May had been removed as leader

explanation.surface: A wry look at the Conservative party's mood after losing its leader Theresa May.
explanation.walkthrough: Theresa May was the UK Conservative (Tory) Prime Minister who resigned in 2019; a party that has lost its May has been 'dis-Mayed'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismayed means discouraged and alarmed, a near synonym of demoralised.

clue.text: Managing to be top

definitions.meaning: getting by, handling a difficult situation
the capping course of stones along the top of a wall

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a builder's word: the sloping layer that finishes off a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Coping is both getting by under pressure and the protective capstone layer on masonry.

clue.text: Get cover quickly behind vehicle

indicators.note: the quick piece comes after the vehicle piece, sitting behind it in the answer

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
apace means swiftly

explanation.surface: An instruction to grab a cover in a hurry from the back of a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A carapace is the hard shell covering a crab or turtle, a protective cover.

clue.text: Like a plant in difficulty — spots show this

parts.note: the clue word spots has the letters P-O-T held between two S's, so it shows a pot enclosed, tied up on both sides

explanation.surface: A gardener describing a struggling plant and pointing to its spotted leaves as proof.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer, read as wordplay, would build the word 'spots' (POT bound by S and S); 'show this' links the two.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant whose roots have filled its container and can no longer grow is described as root-cramped in this way.

clue.text: Short garments — test out the cloth

parts.note: minis are miniskirts, short garments
to try something is to test it out

explanation.surface: Trying on miniskirts to see how the fabric holds up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The cloth' is not fabric: it is the clergy as a body, as in 'a man of the cloth'.
explanation.definitionFit: The clergy collectively are called the cloth, and the ministry is the body of clergy.

clue.text: Namely, loveless idiot

indicators.note: without love: the letter O, love being the zero score in tennis, is taken away

parts.note: to wit means namely

explanation.surface: Someone without love dismissed as a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A twit is a silly, foolish person, a mild British insult.

clue.text: Immature adult — a Parisian lacking discipline

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so the French article is removed from the word for immature

parts.note: young means immature
un is French for a, as a Parisian would say it
A is the film-classification abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: A grown-up child, perhaps a young French person, who has no self-control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a Parisian' looks like a person but is the French article; 'Immature adult' looks like one phrase but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Yoga is a physical and spiritual practice, a discipline in the sense of a regimen of training.

clue.text: Greek character, sailor, about to cross river — the quickest route?

indicators.note: the river letter goes across, sitting inside the turned-round pair
about signals that the Greek letter and sailor are turned round together

parts.note: nu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
tar is a traditional word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A Greek sailor about to cross a river, wondering about the fastest way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the Greek letter and sailor round together, giving RATUN. A rat run is a British term for a minor road used by drivers to dodge traffic.
explanation.definitionFit: A rat run is a back-street shortcut drivers take to avoid congestion, so a supposedly quicker route.

clue.text: Perplexing activity on the cricket field

definitions.meaning: the wicketkeeper's dismissal of a batsman who is out of the crease by breaking the wicket

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the wicketkeeper puts a batsman out by knocking off the bails while the batsman is out of the crease.
explanation.definitionFit: Stumping means baffling, and in cricket a stumping is a mode of dismissal by the wicketkeeper.

clue.text: Support wickedness, bumping off one in proximity

parts.note: a prop is a support

indicators.note: bumping off means killing, so the numeral for one is removed from the wickedness word

parts.note: iniquity means wickedness
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: Backing a wicked plan to kill someone nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bumping off' takes one I out of INIQUITY, leaving INQUITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Propinquity is a formal word for nearness in place or kinship, so closeness or proximity.

clue.text: When in Paris, stars will create difficult situations

parts.note: quand is French for when
Aries is a constellation, a group of stars

explanation.surface: A warning that in Paris the celebrities will cause trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A quandary is a dilemma or predicament, a plight with no clear way out.

clue.text: Slobbering attracted Heather, it's said

indicators.note: it's said signals that the two words are spoken and the sound gives the answer

parts.note: drew means attracted and ling is a name for heather

explanation.surface: Someone salivating over a woman called Heather who caught their eye.
explanation.walkthrough: Heather is not a woman: ling is the plant heather. DREW LING, spoken, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Drooling is letting saliva run from the mouth, the same as slobbering.

clue.text: Jewish historian to tease our sort, penning record

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so the record goes inside the teasing word

parts.note: to josh is to tease
an EP is an extended-play record
us means people like ourselves

explanation.surface: Teasing people like us by writing a record about them.
explanation.definitionFit: Flavius Josephus was the first-century Jewish chronicler of the Jewish War and Antiquities of the Jews.

clue.text: Bar money in famous wedding location

indicators.note: in places the money word inside the place name

parts.note: Cana in Galilee was where, in the Gospel of John, water was turned into wine at a wedding
tin is slang for money

explanation.surface: A bar where cash flows at a famous wedding venue.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantina is a Spanish or Latin American bar or tavern.

clue.text: Oxford literary group in Cambridge college, entertaining learner

indicators.note: entertaining means hosting, so the college holds the learner inside

parts.note: King's is a college of Cambridge University
L is the learner-driver plate letter

explanation.surface: An Oxford writers' circle visiting a Cambridge college and hosting a student.
explanation.walkthrough: The Inklings were the Oxford circle of writers including C. S. Lewis and J. R. R. Tolkien.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inklings were the informal Oxford literary discussion group of Tolkien, Lewis and friends.

clue.text: Perform inadequately as less fancied competitor? Not good

indicators.note: not good says the letter for good must be left off

parts.note: the underdog is the competitor thought less likely to win

explanation.surface: An outsider who fails to shine and is judged not good enough.
explanation.definitionFit: To underdo something is to do it insufficiently, as with undercooked food.

clue.text: Donkey isn't moving with energy — a hard problem

indicators.note: moving means the letters shift into a new order

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A stubborn donkey refuses to move, even with an energy boost, a tough problem for its owner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' rearranges DONKEY and ISNT into KIDNEYSTON; the E for energy closes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A renal calculus is a hard mineral mass in the body, literally a hard problem.

clue.text: Boy that's 5? You've got it!

indicators.note: that's 5 says the boy is in the condition of 5 Down, pot-bound, so he holds a pot inside

parts.note: a son is a boy
5 Down is pot-bound, giving a pot enclosed within

explanation.surface: A cryptic cross-reference followed by a delighted cry of agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 5 Down's answer means 'with a pot bound inside', so a boy in that state holds a pot within him.
explanation.definitionFit: Spot on is an exclamation meaning exactly right, as when someone guesses correctly.

clue.text: Being heartless, get away with trick

indicators.note: heartless removes the central letter of the word for leaving quickly

parts.note: scram means go away quickly

explanation.surface: A cold-hearted person getting away with a con.
explanation.definitionFit: A scam is a swindle or con, a dishonest trick.

clue.text: Good shot brings oppressor to premature end

indicators.note: brought to a premature end means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a bully is an oppressor

explanation.surface: A well-aimed shot finishes off a tyrant early.
explanation.definitionFit: The bull is the bullseye, the centre of a target, so a shot hitting it is a good one.

clue.text: Messengers and companions wasting time

indicators.note: wasting time means the letter for time is lost from the companions word

parts.note: courtiers are attendants, companions of a monarch

explanation.surface: Messengers and their companions idling about.
explanation.definitionFit: Couriers carry packages and messages, so they are messengers.

clue.text: Smooth language

definitions.meaning: to buff or shine a surface

explanation.definitionFit: Polish is both the verb to rub to a shine and the Slavic language of Poland.

clue.text: A gremlin up in the air is a malicious type

indicators.note: up in the air means unsettled, so the letters are thrown into new order

explanation.surface: A gremlin, the mischievous creature blamed for faults in aircraft, flying about as a spiteful sort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up in the air' rearranges A GREMLIN; gremlins were said by RAF airmen to sabotage planes, which fits the airborne surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A maligner is someone who speaks ill of others, a spiteful slanderer.

clue.text: Hooligans attempted to switch sides

indicators.note: to switch means the other edge letter is then carried across to the front
sides points to the two edge letters, the first of which is carried to the far end

parts.note: sought can mean tried or attempted, as in sought to escape

explanation.surface: Thugs who tried to change allegiance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to switch sides' swaps the first and last letters of SOUGHT: S goes to the back (OUGHTS), then T to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Toughs are rough, violent people, thugs or hooligans.
